course_description:
This course is designed to equip final year planning students with understandings, insights and critical thinking to influence their planning practice. The course will make extensive use of case studies.

This course is designed to equip final year planning students with understanding, insights and critical thinking toﾠinfluence their planning practice.ﾠThe course is built around a contemporary statutory planning issue: preparing a planning report for an innovative housing project. Students will have access to experienced planning practitioners as they complete their technical investigations and final report.

Additional timetable information
This course is delivered in weekly 3 hour contact session (2hour lecture and 1 hour practical).ﾠStudents should attend the weekly sessions. It is appreciated that many final year students are working, so all assessment is individual.ﾠ
During Weeks 7-12ﾠa statutory planning skills module will be offered with support of specialist statutory planners.ﾠ Students are required to attend and participate in these sessions (lectures + practicals) to complete the Workbook Module Two and demonstrate the development of the Planning Report.
Some sessions may be offered with an online option via ZOOM/Teams - the guests may join us via Zoom/Teams. Practical activities are skills-based and have been designed to be completed in-person.
We will monitor in-person attendance and session format may be adjusted over the semester. Student attendance and progress on Assessment 2 will be monitored in Weeks 7 -11, and an 80% attendance is required to contribute to the Identity Verified Assessment requirement for the course.
In Week 6, a COMPULSORY 2-day field trip will be held on Monday 31 August - Tuesday 1 September 2026. The field trip has been co-designed with industry stakeholders and will showcase challenges for planning and development practice in Brisbane City and Southeast Queensland. Online resources will be available to support engagement and transfer of industry insights. These resources will be posted on Blackboard.
course_aims: This course will provide students with advanced-level practical skills and expertise so that they can contribute competently to complex professional situations that are likely to be encountered in the work place through the use of extensive up to date case studies and practical tasks.

learning_outcomes.description: Review and analyse the principles and concepts that underpin the planning profession and planning practice.
Breakdown and address complex planning issues
Navigate and review a planning scheme and develop planning solutions to a complex development theme.
Demonstrate an appreciation of the ethics and ethical standards of the planning profession.
Summarise and explain the role of planners working independently and in multi-disciplinary teams.
Prepare a professional planning report for local development project.

assessment_details.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Notebook/ Logbook, Participation/ Student contribution, Practical/ Demonstration, Presentation, Reflection
assessment_details.due_date: Digital Submission: Presentation Slides 14/10/2026 2:00 pm Presentation 15/10/2026 2:00 pm Digital Submission: Workbook 16/10/2026 2:00 pm Oral Presentation: Timetabled within Week 11 Working Session.
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale Skills Module Two focuses on the application of statutory planning concepts, legislation, and planning tools. Students are required to critically analyse development proposals within the Queensland planning system and demonstrate their understanding through the completion of workbook activities, culminating in a professional presentation and question-and-answer session with the class. This assessment involves: Attendance and active participation in a series of weekly workshops with a statutory planning specialist. Through these sessions, students will develop foundational knowledge and practical skills in statutory planning and development assessment. Student attendance at these sessions will be tracked. Completion and submission of an individual workbook that documents and reflects on activities undertaken during the workshops (Weeks 6–10). A professional presentation in Week 11, in which students will analyse the statutory planning issues associated with an assigned development scenario. Presentations will be five minutes in length and supported by presentation slides. Participation in a question-and-answer session, where students will be required to explain and defend their analysis. Completion of Skills Module Two includes three components: Presentation Slides (25%), Presentation (25%) and Workbook (50%). These individual components are submitted and completed over three days in Week 11. Guidance on the presentation structure, analytical framework, and graphic requirements will be provided via Blackboard. The workbook will be made available in Week 7 and can be accessed through Blackboard. assessment_details.title: Assessment 3: Planning Report and Reflection
assessment_details.due_date: Planning Report and Reflection 13/11/2026 2:00 pm Digital Submission: via Blackboard.
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale This is an individual assessment in which you will prepare a Planning Report for an innovative development proposal. Due to the project's design, location, and potential impacts, the proposal is considered impact assessable and requires development approval under the Queensland planning system. The project should demonstrate leading practice in addressing one or more strategic planning priorities, including (but not limited to): Affordable housing Climate-responsive design Liveability Students must select a development proposal and site from the list provided on Blackboard. A report template will also be provided for students to follow. This assessment is in two parts: Planning Report (90%) - A professional planning report that critically assesses and justifies the proposed development against the Queensland Planning System. The report must not exceed 5,000 words, including quotations. The word limit does not include appendices, tables, or the application form completed using the relevant Queensland Government templates. Practice Reflection (10%) - An individual reflection that demonstrates your learning and professional development throughout the project. The reflection must follow the structure and requirements provided on Blackboard. Further assessment details, including submission requirements and supporting resources, are available on Blackboard.
